text: Parvovirus is the most common cause of infertility in pigs and is present on essentially all farms. A gilt/sow infected for the first time while not pregnant shows no clinical signs. In pregnant sows: infection between day 0–35 of gestation kills some fetuses, which are fully reabsorbed, resulting in small litters (4–5 piglets) or repeat breeding if all embryos die; infection after day 35 (once bones have started forming) causes mummification instead, with the virus progressing slowly piglet to piglet so mummies of varying size (30–160 mm) appear at birth. Abortion is not typically seen with Parvovirus. Treatment: none. Prevention: vaccinate gilts and sows 10–15 days before mating/AI — gilts need 2 shots (e.g. at 6.5 and 7.5 months if first mating is planned around 8 months); sows are vaccinated 1 week before weaning.
